summary:
What if an alien discovered a planet that never stops dancing?

ZORI's Alien Earth Observatory is an interactive platform that brings Earth's hidden changes to life using real NASA–ISRO NISAR radar data.

ZORI lets users explore a 3D globe, investigate changes in water, forests, and ground motion, and visualize authentic satellite measurements through interactive comparisons.

An original animated alien guide makes complex science simple and exciting, with six languages and explanations for beginners and future scientists.

ZORI's mission is to make Earth observation accessible to everyone — inspiring curiosity, supporting education, and helping people explore environmental changes using real scientific evidence.

Earth never stops dancing. ZORI helps us understand its movements.
details:
What if an alien could help us decode Earth's hidden signals?

ZORI's Alien Earth Observatory transforms real NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite data into an interactive journey through our changing planet.

Users explore a 3D globe, select locations and time periods, and investigate real satellite observations. ZORI searches NASA's Alaska Satellite Facility archive and processes authentic NISAR GCOV radar backscatter and GUNW interferometric data, revealing signals related to changes in water, vegetation, and ground motion through interactive scientific visualizations.

What makes ZORI unique is its ability to make complex science feel simple and exciting. My original animated alien character guides visitors through discoveries using storytelling, six languages, and explanations at three levels — from beginner to scientist.

Built with Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, MapLibre GL JS, NumPy, SciPy, and h5py, ZORI runs on Google Cloud Run.

The potential impact goes beyond education. ZORI can help teachers introduce real satellite research into classrooms, inspire students to become future scientists, and empower communities to explore environmental changes affecting their regions — without requiring advanced technical expertise.

Scientific accuracy, accessibility, and transparency are central to the design. Radar signals are explained with their limitations rather than presented as confirmed disasters.

My next step is to transform ZORI into an AI-powered Earth science companion that answers questions, guides investigations, and helps people develop their own scientific understanding using trustworthy satellite data.

Today, ZORI helps us discover Earth's hidden movements. Tomorrow, it could help anyone become an explorer of our changing planet.
